answer: Because the island release is entered with every signature, the timber audit makes public the quorum and a forged release is rejected on replay. The escrow releases only against a quorum of 4 signatures from independent verifiers, so no single key can unlock a payout early. A farm that controls the author cannot also supply the quorum, because each signer must be independent on the voyage graph and each risks its bond. That is 22 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
